newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-ITALY TAKE SURPRISE 1-0 LEAD OVER SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ITALY TAKE SURPRISE 1-0 LEAD OVER SPAIN.

text.p: Italy produced an early surprise on Friday when Omar Camporese gave them a 1-0 lead over heavily-fancied Spain in their Davis Cup world group quarter-final.
In a battle lasting three hours and 39 minutes, the veteran Italian number two belied the notion that the hosts might succumb meekly with a remarkable comeback against Spanish number one Carlos Moya.

Moya, ranked eighth in the world, struggled to win the first two sets on tie-breaks before Camporese, ranked 156th, turned the match on its head to take the final three sets and win by 6-7 (8-10) 6-7 (4-7) 6-1 6-3 6-3.

The Italians had done their best to cast Spain as the overwhelming favourites, with captain Adriano Panatta even going so far as to give his men no more than a 20 percent chance against a team with two men in the world's top 20.
"They have an 80 percent chance of winning and we have 20 percent. That seems to me a realistic forecast," said Panatta.
